about: Research record for the base-site sunlight data added on 2026-10-23 (data agent, second judging round). Every quote below was checked by script to appear in the page, abstract or PDS label fetched on that date. LOLA illumination values: scripts/extract_illumination.py (summary data/illumination.json; 5x5 windows and the PDS label text in data/raw/illumination/).

sources.usedFor: the 'Sunlight (LOLA)', 'Earth in view (LOLA)' and 'Nearest permanent shadow (LOLA)' facts of malapert, mons-mouton and shackleton-ridge
quotes: This data product is a map of the average illumination by the solar disc of the Lunar South Pole at a resolution of 60 m/pix by 60 m/pix
The values are continuous between 0 (permanent shadow) and 1, and indicate the percentage of timesteps where each pixel was sunlit (by any fraction of the solar disc).
This data product is a map of the permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) in the lunar South Pole.
As with all EXTRAs products, these files are not supported by the PDS or the LOLA Science Team.

searchedNotFound.sp-crater-sfvf regolith: No source documents SP Crater's own material as a regolith simulant or building material. The JSC-1/1A simulants come from Merriam Crater (about 40 km away) and BP-1 from the Black Point lava flow, both in the same volcanic field but not SP Crater. Tag removed under the regolith rule.
searchedNotFound.malapert regolith: Kring et al. 2025 (doi 10.1029/2024JE008905) lists 'regolith physical properties' as a goal of planned EVAs, not as a measurement at the summit. No tag.
searchedNotFound.mons-mouton / shackleton-ridge regolith: No source documents regolith at these pins. General south-polar statements do not count (same rule as the crater floor). No tag.
searchedNotFound.base-site ice: The LOLA maps give the distance to the nearest permanently shadowed pixel, but a shadowed place is where ice can stay, not detected ice. No ice tag (the resources rule needs ice documented at the target).
